business_problem: JEVS Human Services had outgrown a shallow ticketing system, leaving programs to manage incidents and client-facing cases through separate workflows without a central record, enough automation, or the compliance controls required for sensitive social-service information.
solution_summary: JEVS implemented ServiceNow IT Service Management and case management as a unified system of record for youth employment, senior services, disability support, and other programs. The platform was designed around human-in-the-loop handling so personally identifiable information stays controlled even as automation expands. Staff were trained through ServiceNow University and pro bono ServiceNow volunteering so the nonprofit could sustain the platform internally instead of treating it as a one-time deployment. Once live, ServiceNow centralized case and incident activity from eight programs and divisions, integrated that record with JEVS' data warehouse, and automated most routine work with template responses, workflow routing, and audit-ready tracking. The same foundation now supports thousands of prospective clients through application and onboarding flows, and JEVS is preparing self-service portals and AI agents for low-priority incidents that do not carry regulatory restrictions.

solution_components.name: IT Service Management
solution_components.role: Acts as JEVS' centralized incident and service workflow platform across multiple programs.

solution_components.name: Case management
solution_components.role: Tracks external-client and program workflows on the same system of record as internal incidents.

solution_components.name: ServiceNow University
solution_components.role: Builds internal practitioner capability so JEVS can maintain and optimize the platform over time.

data_flow: Incidents and client inquiries from multiple programs flow into one ServiceNow record, where routing, template responses, and automated handling resolve routine work first. The resulting case data is then integrated with JEVS' data warehouse, while staff continue to manage complex or sensitive situations with human oversight and audit-ready tracking.
business_outcome: JEVS moved nearly 98% of inquiries to resolved or closed status, automated 75% of routine work, cut unaddressed tickets from 40% to 10%, enabled lean teams to handle up to 300 inquiries per day, and created a centralized record that scales across more than two dozen programs serving 18,000 people annually.
architecture_clues: The deployment spans eight programs and divisions and integrates with the organization's broader data warehouse.
Human-in-the-loop workflows were prioritized for use cases involving PII such as social security numbers and government IDs.
JEVS trained 24 users across five departments and developed four internal ServiceNow practitioners.
evidence_quotes: JEVS made the decision to implement ServiceNow IT Service Management and case management to support these expanding programs.
The implementation prioritized human-in-the-loop workflows from the start, especially for sensitive use cases requiring careful management of personally identifiable information (PII).
JEVS also leveraged ServiceNow University to train staff on the platform.
Now, 75% of routine cases are handled through automation while human staff focus on the complex cases that require judgment and empathy.
The system has created a centralized place for numerous programs without a unified system of record to integrate with JEVS's broader data warehouse.
